question: What is the primary function of a water distribution main?

To remove suspended solids from raw water
To disinfect water at the treatment plant

Trunk sewer

correctAnswer: At a dead end with long detention time

Just downstream of the treatment plant
Beside an elevated tank that turns over daily
At a large, steady industrial user

To test customer meters

explanation: A healthy pressure reducing valve holds its set downstream pressure at all flows. Pressure that rises when flow is low points to the valve passing water it should be holding back.
options: Night time demand in the lower zone is higher than daytime demand
At low night flows the valve is not controlling properly, for example from a worn seat, letting higher zone pressure bleed into the lower zone
The elevated tank drains completely every night and refills by morning
Customer water heaters across the lower zone all run at the same hour
optionA: Night time demand in the lower zone is higher than daytime demand
optionB: At low night flows the valve is not controlling properly, for example from a worn seat, letting higher zone pressure bleed into the lower zone
optionC: The elevated tank drains completely every night and refills by morning
optionD: Customer water heaters across the lower zone all run at the same hour

question: An inspector finds large patches of failed coating with rust breaking through on the inside wall of a steel tank near the waterline. Why is recoating scheduled rather than leaving it for the next inspection cycle?

question: A routine distribution sample returns an adverse microbiological result. What is the key duty that follows under Ontario Regulation 170/03?

Report the result as required and take the required corrective action
Discard the result if no customer has complained
Record it only if the same tap fails again next year

question: Why does Ontario Regulation 170/03 require sampling and testing in the distribution system?
correctAnswer: To verify that water quality is maintained throughout the system and to detect problems early

question: How should records that Ontario Regulation 170/03 requires for distribution operations be handled?

Documenting checks only when a result looks unusual

question: Which older service line material is a concern because it can contribute lead to a customer's drinking water?

Cross-linked polyethylene
Lead

question: A newer residential service line is flexible plastic tubing that resists corrosion. It is most likely made of which material?
correctAnswer: Cross-linked polyethylene, commonly called PEX

Cast iron

question: Why can an ageing galvanized steel service line cause low flow at a customer's taps?
correctAnswer: Internal corrosion and buildup narrow the inside of the pipe over time

options: Internal corrosion and buildup narrow the inside of the pipe over time
The pipe slowly turns transparent and leaks light
The pipe produces chlorine that blocks the tap
The pipe expands until it presses on the meter

question: Copper service lines have been widely used mainly because copper is which of the following?
correctAnswer: Durable and resistant to corrosion when water chemistry is suitable

question: During an excavation, a crew exposes a service line of unknown material. What is the best practice before backfilling?
correctAnswer: Identify the material and record it in the system's service records
explanation: Identifying and recording the material while it is exposed builds an accurate inventory, which matters for lead awareness and future work.

Ignore it, because only the main matters
Paint it blue so the next crew can guess

question: Shortly after a main break repair on the next street, a customer reports reddish brown water. What is the most likely cause and the best first response?

explanation: Flow changes during a break and repair stir up iron sediment. Checking the area pattern and flushing the affected section addresses the usual cause.
options: Iron sediment disturbed by changed flows, so check for related events in the area and arrange flushing if needed
Sewage entering the main, so tell the customer to stop using water for a week
Algae growing in the service line, so dose the service with extra chlorine
Sand from a quarry, so replace the customer's plumbing

question: A customer says the water tastes strongly of chlorine. What should the operator do before deciding anything needs to change?
correctAnswer: Test the chlorine residual at a suitable tap rather than relying on taste alone

Test the chlorine residual at a suitable tap rather than relying on taste alone
Tell the customer that taste proves the water is contaminated

question: Several taste and odour complaints come from one dead end street, while the rest of the zone reports nothing. What is the best investigation step?
correctAnswer: Sample the residual in that area and inspect and flush the dead end section

options: Wait a month to see whether the complaints stop on their own
Raise the chlorine dose for the whole system
Replace every service line on the street first
Sample the residual in that area and inspect and flush the dead end section

question: A customer fills a glass and sees milky white water that clears from the bottom upward within a minute. What is the most likely explanation?

Colonies of bacteria that sink when disturbed

Only the cost of the visit

question: In a distribution system, a SCADA system is mainly used to do what?
correctAnswer: Monitor conditions and control equipment such as pumps and tank levels from a central location
explanation: SCADA gathers data from field instruments and lets operators monitor and control pumps, valves, and storage remotely.

Test bacteriological samples automatically
Monitor conditions and control equipment such as pumps and tank levels from a central location
Bill customers for their water use

question: SCADA shows an elevated tank level falling quickly even though the fill pumps show running and demand is normal. What should the operator do?

Silence the alarm and check again next week
Assume the tank gauge is always wrong
Shut down the whole distribution system at once

correctAnswer: Trends show patterns over time, such as night flows that stay high when demand should be low
